$comment: Benchmark tasks. Prompts are phrased as a product engineer would ask and never name envUI components. Each capability lists the envUI exports that provide it (any one covers it; 'Component.prop' means that component used with that prop), or, under 'rendered', checks of what the browser step renders: a capability is covered when every check passes at its widths ('at', all four by default), in its state ('loaded' by default, or 'loading', right after the app first renders). Anchors find visible elements by their text or aria-label, case-insensitively, or the nearest element around it that matches 'within'. A task with 'pending' runs only when named in --tasks: it waits for an envUI API that doesn't exist yet.

tasks.title: Collapsible sidebar with a toggle
tasks.prompt: Add a collapsible sidebar to the app with navigation links for Projects, Members and Settings; Projects is the current page. Put a button at the top that collapses and expands the sidebar, and remember whether it was collapsed between visits.

tasks.title: Settings form
tasks.prompt: Add a Settings page for the workspace in src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx and show it in App.tsx below the projects page. It is a form with the workspace name, a description, a time zone picked from a short list, and an on/off option for email notifications. Add Save and Cancel buttons: Save calls `saveSettings` from `src/api.ts`, Cancel resets the form.

tasks.title: Filterable, sortable table with an empty state
tasks.prompt: Show the projects as a table with columns for name, owner, status and last updated. Add a search box above it that filters by project name, let people sort by clicking the column headers, and when no project matches the search show a friendly empty state with a button that clears the search.

tasks.title: Confirm-delete flow
tasks.prompt: Add a way to delete a project from the projects list. Deleting must ask for confirmation first, naming the project, and only call `deleteProject` from `src/api.ts` after the user confirms; then remove the project from the list.

tasks.title: Toast after saving
tasks.prompt: Let people rename a project: add a small inline rename form (a name field and a Save button) to each project in the list. Saving calls `renameProject` from `src/api.ts`. After it saves, show a success toast that disappears on its own; if saving fails, show an error toast instead.

tasks.title: Page header with breadcrumbs and actions
tasks.prompt: Give the projects page a proper page header: breadcrumbs (Home > Projects), the page title with the number of projects shown next to it, and two actions on the right, 'Export' and 'New project' (they can just log to the console for now).

tasks.title: Command palette with a keyboard shortcut
tasks.prompt: Add a quick search: pressing Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on macOS) opens a search over the page that lists all projects, filters them as you type and works with the arrow keys and Enter. Choosing a project shows it as the selected project at the top of the projects page. Also add a search button to the header that shows the shortcut and opens the same search.

tasks.title: Tabs with a badge count
tasks.prompt: Split the projects page into tabs for Active, Paused and Archived projects. Each tab label shows how many projects are in it.

tasks.title: Account menu from an avatar
tasks.prompt: Add an account menu at the right end of the header. It shows the signed-in user's avatar (`currentUser` from `src/data/members.ts`); clicking it opens a menu with the user's name and email at the top, followed by 'Profile', 'Settings' and 'Sign out'.

tasks.title: File upload drop area
tasks.prompt: Add an attachments section below the projects list where people can drag and drop files or browse for them. List the chosen files with their name and size, let people remove a file before uploading, and add an Upload button that sends them with `uploadFiles` from `src/api.ts` and shows that it is working while it uploads.

tasks.title: Date picker in a form
tasks.prompt: Add a 'New milestone' form to the projects page with a project chosen from the existing projects, a title, a due date picked from a calendar, an optional description and a Create button. Dates in the past must not be selectable. On submit, call `createMilestone` from `src/api.ts`.

tasks.title: Loading state with skeletons
tasks.prompt: Load the projects with `fetchProjects()` from `src/api.ts` instead of importing the sample data directly. While they load, show placeholder rows in the shape of the list; if loading fails, show an error message with a Retry button.

tasks.title: Inline alert
tasks.prompt: At the top of the projects page, tell people that the workspace is on the free plan, which allows up to 10 projects, with an 'Upgrade' link to /billing. Make it a warning once there are 8 or more projects, and let people dismiss it.

tasks.title: App frame with navigation that changes with the width
tasks.prompt: Give the app a proper frame. Keep the app's name, Workspace, at the top, and add navigation to three destinations, Projects, Members and Settings, each with an icon; Projects is the current one, and the projects page stays the content. How the navigation shows depends on the room the app has: on a phone-sized window it is a bar along the bottom with icons and labels; on a tablet-sized window a narrow strip down the left side with icons and short labels; on a wide window a list down the left side with full labels. The content uses the rest of the space.

capabilities.label: navigation to Projects, Members and Settings at every width
a bar below the content on a phone
a narrow strip beside the content on a tablet
a list beside the content on a wide window

tasks.title: Dashboard of summary cards and a grid of project cards
tasks.prompt: Add an overview to the top of the projects page: four summary cards titled Active projects, Paused projects, Archived projects and Open tasks, each showing its number, worked out from the sample data. On a wide window the four cards sit in one row; on a tablet-sized window they form two rows of two; on a phone they stack in one column. Below the overview, show the projects as cards with their name, owner and status, in a grid that fits as many columns as there is room for: at least three on a wide window, and one on a phone.

capabilities.label: four summary cards in one row on a wide window
two rows of two on a tablet
project cards in as many columns as fit

tasks.title: List and detail of projects
tasks.prompt: Turn the projects page into a list and detail view. The list shows every project's name; choosing one shows its details: the name as a heading, then the owner, the status, the number of open tasks and when it was last updated, each with a label (Owner, Status, Open tasks, Last updated). Start with the first project selected. On a wide window the list and the details sit side by side; on a phone show one at a time, the list first, with a way back to the list from the details.

capabilities.label: the selected project's details with their labels
list and details side by side on a wide window
one pane at a time on a phone

tasks.title: Settings page in a readable column
tasks.prompt: Add a Settings page in src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx and show it in App.tsx in place of the projects page. It has the heading 'Workspace settings' and a form with the workspace name, a description, a time zone picked from a short list and an on/off option for email notifications, then Save and Cancel buttons (they can log to the console). Lay the form out in a readable column: on a wide window it doesn't stretch across the screen but keeps a comfortable reading width and is centered; on a phone it uses the full width with small margins.

capabilities.label: a readable, centered column on a wide window
the full width with small margins on a phone

tasks.title: Project cards that load in their own shape
tasks.pending: Waits for envUI's skeleton API: a skeleton prop on surfaces and placeholder items. Card.skeleton, Surface.skeleton, ListItem.skeleton and placeholders are the names the plan gives; check them when the API lands.
tasks.prompt: Load the projects with `fetchProjects()` from `src/api.ts` instead of importing the sample data directly, and show them as cards with the name, the owner, the status and the number of open tasks. While they load, show the same cards in a loading shape, roughly like the real ones (three of them), rather than a spinner. If loading fails, show an error message with a Retry button.

capabilities.label: the cards themselves as skeletons while loading
placeholder items rendered with the same components

tasks.title: Loading state for content of unknown shape
tasks.pending: Waits for envUI's skeleton API, which keeps LoadingState for content of unknown shape; check the names when the API lands.
tasks.prompt: Add an Activity section below the projects list that loads the workspace's latest activity with `fetchActivity()` from `src/api.ts`. The activity is free text whose length and paragraphs vary, so while it loads, show that it is loading with a short message instead of imitating its shape; then show the text.

capabilities.label: a loading indicator with a message
